crime_highlights: Mr. Izzard intervened. He argued with the victim.
She moved away and he followed her and stabbed her in the back
The victim suffered a one-and-a-half-inch stab wound to the centre left of the spine
rationale_highlights: in consequence, at least in part, of his Indigenous and racialized background
It is clear that Mr. Izzard's history contributed to the criminal conduct in this case.
history mitigates, though it does not eliminate, his moral culpability
A sentence of just three years, as opposed to the longer sentence imposed by the judge, is justified by the reduction in Mr. Izzard's moral blameworthiness
note: Crime passage has little on victim effects; fear for her life is in para 53.

crime_highlights: All of the robberies involved the use of an imitation firearm, and several included terrifying threats to the employees
He approached the customer service person, pointed a handgun at them
He again produced a firearm, demanded $10,000, and threatened to shoot people if he did not get the money
rationale_highlights: bear minimally on his moral blameworthiness
I accept that the effects of colonialism on Mr. Billy have been both profound and direct.
that these factors have resulted in dysfunction in First Nation communities and that they must be given particular attention in determining a fit sentence
note: Court found Gladue factors bore minimally on culpability; appeal court says effects profound and direct.

crime_highlights: They removed some items from the house then poured gas throughout
the appellant and his mother planned to set the fire together
the heat from the flames melted the siding of a neighbour's house and the appellant's residence was destroyed
rationale_highlights: suffered the intergenerational effects of colonialism
Indigenous sentencing factors and his mental health issues mitigated his moral blameworthiness
The judge accepted the appellant's reduced moral blameworthiness.
note: Para 11 narrative is in crime passage; no victim injuries, only property damage and danger.
